name: information-and-controls
title: Information and controls, presented together
kicker: Fielding, in the comments on his 2008 post
html:
Information and controls, presented together

“When I say hypertext, I mean the simultaneous presentation of information and controls such that the information becomes the affordance through which the user (or automaton) obtains choices and selects actions.”

Roy T. Fielding, comment, 20 October 2008

information
+
controls
=
affordance

On the human web they were married: the page and its forms arrive together. This is what lets an infer-once replay survive change.
say: This is the marriage. On the human web, the page and its forms arrive together; the information itself is how you find out what you can do. And this is what lets Hightower's infer-once replay survive change: the controls come with every answer, so the replay can check them for free.

deck:ref.name: hypertext
deck:ref.label: “When I say hypertext…”
deck:ref.title: What hypertext means
deck:ref.summary: His definition: information and controls, presented together. Machines can follow links too.
deck:ref.quote:
“When I say hypertext, I mean the simultaneous presentation of information and controls such that the information becomes the affordance through which the user (or automaton) obtains choices and selects actions. Hypermedia is just an expansion on what text means to include temporal anchors within a media stream; most researchers have dropped the distinction.

Hypertext does not need to be HTML on a browser. Machines can follow links when they understand the data format and relationship types.”
deck:ref.cite: Roy T. Fielding, comment on “REST APIs must be hypertext-driven”
